description: Types of digital communication, the software and devices used to create them, and the channels that deliver them.
hero_image_caption: A content creator filming a video for digital distribution using a smartphone and lighting equipment.
content_html:
What Are Digital Communications?

Digital communications are the messages, content and information that organisations and individuals create and share using digital technology. The spec lists eleven types: audio, collaboration tools, leaflets, infographics, newsletters, presentations, reports, social media, video, Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) and websites. For each type, you must know its purpose, advantages, disadvantages and when it is the most suitable choice.

Key Fact

The eleven communication types are: audio, collaboration tools, leaflet, infographics, newsletters, presentations, reports, social media, video, VoIP and websites. Each has a specific purpose that makes it the best choice in certain contexts but not others.

Key Communication Types and Their Purposes

Audio (podcasts, audio adverts, voice messages) communicates without visuals — useful for on-the-go consumption (commuters, gym users) but cannot convey diagrams or visual data. Video combines moving images, audio and text — highly engaging and suited to demonstrations, tutorials and marketing, but expensive and time-consuming to produce and requires fast internet to stream. Infographics present data and statistics visually using charts, icons and minimal text — excellent for making complex data memorable and shareable on social media, but oversimplification can reduce accuracy.

Collaboration tools enable teams to work together remotely in real time — editing shared documents, tracking tasks or running virtual meetings. VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) transmits voice calls over the internet rather than a traditional phone network — it is cheaper for international calls but depends on a stable internet connection. Social media enables rapid, two-way communication with large audiences at low cost, but content can spread inaccurate information quickly and organisations lose some control over how their message is interpreted.

Newsletters deliver regular updates directly to subscribers — a targeted audience who have opted in — making them effective for maintaining customer relationships, but open rates decline if content is not relevant. Websites provide a permanent, accessible home for information that any user can find at any time. Leaflets in digital form are PDF documents or email attachments that work like printed leaflets but can be distributed cheaply via email or download. Presentations support verbal communication with slides — effective in meetings or events but require a presenter to add context. Reports provide structured, detailed information for decision-making — less engaging but highly credible for formal audiences.

Desktop publishing (DTP) software is designed for creating visually rich documents like leaflets, infographics, newsletters and reports. It offers precise control over layout, typography, images and colour. Standard office applications (word processors, presentation tools, spreadsheets) are more widely available and familiar but offer less design control than DTP software. For the exam, you need to select and justify the most appropriate software for a given scenario.

The five named digital devices are: smartphone (portable, always connected, suited to social media, messaging, VoIP and consuming audio/video content on the move); smart TV (large screen, suited to streaming video and presenting visual content to groups); PC/laptop (full keyboard and screen, suited to creating detailed reports, presentations and websites); tablet (portable, touchscreen, suited to presenting content in meetings or accessing collaboration tools); smartboard (interactive display used in classrooms and meeting rooms for presentations and collaborative tools). Select the most suitable device by matching its characteristics to the context described in the scenario.

Distribution Channels and Connectivity

Distribution channels are how content reaches its audience. The seven named channels are: cloud (content stored and accessed via online platforms), email (direct, targeted delivery to known recipients), messaging (instant text-based communication for individuals or groups), mobile apps (branded app experiences), multimedia platforms (video/audio hosting and streaming), VoIP (internet voice/video calls) and websites (publicly accessible, searchable).

Each channel works over a connectivity method. Wired connections (Ethernet cable) offer high speed and reliability but require physical infrastructure. Wi-Fi provides wireless connectivity within a building. Bluetooth connects devices at short range (typically up to 10 metres) and is used for peripherals and file transfer. 4G/5G mobile networks allow internet access away from Wi-Fi hotspots. Mobile Wi-Fi hotspots use a mobile data connection to create a portable Wi-Fi network that other devices can join. Selecting the right connectivity method depends on range, speed, cost and whether the user is in a fixed or mobile location.

The spec requires you to match a communication type, distribution channel and connectivity method to a specific audience demographic. The four demographic factors are: accessibility (can the audience use the format — does it need assistive technology, large text, or caption support?), age (younger users may prefer social media and mobile apps; older users may prefer email or printed leaflets), gender (some platforms attract different audience profiles — relevant for targeted marketing) and location (a rural audience with limited broadband may need content that works over mobile data; an international audience may need VoIP rather than phone calls).

For example: a charity campaign targeting 18–25 year olds in urban areas to recruit volunteers would suit social media posts (communication type), mobile app distribution (channel) over 4G/5G (connectivity) — because the demographic is mobile-first, uses social platforms heavily, and may be on the move when they see the campaign. An annual financial report for company shareholders would suit a formal report (communication type), emailed as a PDF (channel) over wired broadband (connectivity) — because the audience expects detailed, credible data and likely accesses it on a desk computer.

Key Fact

The seven distribution channels are: cloud, email, messaging, mobile apps, multimedia, VoIP and websites. The five connectivity methods are: wired, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, 4G/5G and mobile Wi-Fi hotspots. Always match your choice to the audience’s location, device, age and accessibility needs.
exam_tip_html: For the 8-mark “create” question in this topic, you may be asked to sketch a diagram showing how a digital communication reaches its target audience — for example, mapping the communication type, software used, device, distribution channel and connectivity. Label every box and arrow clearly, and make sure every element connects back to the scenario. A common mistake is drawing a generic diagram without naming the specific communication type, device or channel the scenario mentions — this loses the scenario-link marks. For extended response questions, justify your choices: “I chose email because the audience is over 50, so they are more likely to use email than social media.”
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • Eleven digital communication types (audio, collaboration tools, leaflet, infographic, newsletter, presentation, report, social media, video, VoIP, website) each have specific purposes, advantages and disadvantages — the right choice depends on the context and audience.
  • Software (DTP or standard office) and five digital devices (smartphone, smart TV, PC/laptop, tablet, smartboard) are used to create and present communications — match the device to the scenario's requirements.
  • Seven distribution channels (cloud, email, messaging, mobile apps, multimedia, VoIP, websites) deliver content over five connectivity methods (wired, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, 4G/5G, mobile Wi-Fi hotspot) — audience demographics (accessibility, age, gender, location) determine the best combination.

practice_questions.text: On the page, sketch a diagram showing how a small restaurant could use digital communications to promote a new menu to local customers. Your diagram should include: the communication type(s) chosen; the software or device used to create and send them; the distribution channel(s); the connectivity method; and a clear link to the local restaurant scenario throughout.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (7–8): at least two labelled communication types appropriate to a local restaurant (e.g. social media post, email newsletter, website update) (1); software or device labelled for each (e.g. smartphone app for social media, PC with office software for newsletter) (2); distribution channel labelled for each type (e.g. social media platform, email, website) (1); connectivity method included (e.g. Wi-Fi or mobile data/4G) (1); clear directional flow from creation to audience (1); all elements linked to local restaurant scenario (1); overall completeness and clarity (1).
Secure (5–6): most criteria met; minor omissions in connectivity or scenario links.
Developing (3–4): some labelled elements; distribution channel or connectivity missing.
Emerging (1–2): minimal labelled attempt.
0: no creditworthy attempt.

practice_questions.text: State one advantage of using video as a digital communication type.
practice_questions.marks: 1 mark: any one of — highly engaging because it combines visuals, audio and motion (1); effective for demonstrating a product or process step by step (1); easy to share across social media and multimedia platforms, reaching a large audience quickly (1). Accept any clearly stated, relevant advantage.

practice_questions.text: Describe two characteristics of a smartphone that make it suitable for distributing digital communications to a mobile audience.
practice_questions.marks: 2 marks, one per characteristic: portable — users carry it constantly, so they receive push notifications and messages at any time and place (1); connected to 4G/5G mobile networks — the user can access content even without a Wi-Fi connection, making it suitable for audiences on the move (1). Accept other clearly described relevant characteristics such as touchscreen interaction or built-in camera for content creation.

practice_questions.text: Explain why a charity targeting elderly donors in rural areas might choose email distribution over social media distribution.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (3): identifies a relevant demographic factor (age — older users are less likely to use social media platforms) (1); explains this in context (so email is more likely to reach the intended audience because older users are familiar with and regularly check email) (1); adds a second supporting reason (rural location means mobile data coverage may be weaker, but email works reliably over a wired home broadband connection that rural users are more likely to have than consistent 4G/5G) (1).
Secure (2): two points, one with explanation but not fully developed.
Developing (1): names email and social media with a vague reference to age without explaining why.
Emerging (0): no creditworthy content.

practice_questions.text: Outline the difference between Desktop Publishing software and standard office applications for creating digital communications.
practice_questions.marks: 2 marks: DTP software is designed specifically for layout-intensive documents and offers precise control over typography, image placement and colour (1); standard office applications are more widely available and familiar to users but offer less design control and are better suited to documents where structure and content are more important than precise visual design (1).

practice_questions.text: Describe four factors a digital marketing team should consider when selecting a distribution channel and connectivity method for a campaign targeting 16–24-year-old students in a city.
practice_questions.marks: 4 marks, 1 per described factor linked to the demographic. Accept any four: age — 16–24-year-olds heavily use mobile apps and social media platforms, so a mobile app or social media channel is appropriate (1); location (urban) — strong 4G/5G and Wi-Fi coverage in cities means mobile data or Wi-Fi connectivity will work reliably, enabling video and interactive content (1); device preference — this demographic predominantly uses smartphones, so the channel must be mobile-optimised with app notifications or social media feeds (1); accessibility — ensure content has captions or alternative text for students who rely on assistive technology (1); cost — students may use free platforms rather than subscribing to services, so free distribution channels (social media, website) are more likely to reach them (1). Award marks for any four clearly described, context-linked factors.

knowledge_checks.q: Which digital communication type is specifically designed to present data visually using charts and icons with minimal text?
Which connectivity method connects devices wirelessly over a short range of approximately 10 metres?
_____ software is designed for creating visually rich documents like leaflets and newsletters, giving precise control over layout, typography and images.
Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) transmits voice calls over the _____ rather than a traditional phone network, making it cheaper for international calls.
Match each digital device to its most suitable communication use case.
right: Presenting content in meetings using a touchscreen interface
Interactive display for group presentations in a classroom
Streaming video content on a large screen for a shared audience
On-the-go access to social media, VoIP and messaging

flashcard_questions.a: Voice over Internet Protocol — transmitting voice calls over the internet.

flashcard_questions.q: Name the eleven types of digital communication in the spec.
flashcard_questions.a: Audio, collaboration tools, leaflet, infographic, newsletter, presentation, report, social media, video, VoIP, website.
Digital tools allowing multiple people to work on the same document or project in real time.

flashcard_questions.q: Name the five digital devices in the spec.
flashcard_questions.a: Smartphone, smart TV, PC/laptop, tablet, smartboard.

flashcard_questions.q: Name the seven distribution channels in the spec.
flashcard_questions.a: Cloud, email, messaging, mobile apps, multimedia, VoIP, websites.

flashcard_questions.q: Name the five connectivity methods in the spec.
flashcard_questions.a: Wired, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, 4G/5G, mobile Wi-Fi hotspots.

flashcard_questions.q: What four audience demographic factors affect the choice of distribution channel?
Give one advantage of wired connectivity over Wi-Fi.
flashcard_questions.a: Higher speed and more reliable — no signal interference.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot?
flashcard_questions.a: A device that uses mobile data to create a portable Wi-Fi network for other devices.

flashcard_questions.q: Give one advantage of infographics over reports.
flashcard_questions.a: Present data visually and memorably; easier to share on social media.

glossary_terms.definition: Information created and delivered in digital formats, including audio, video, infographics, newsletters, presentations, social media posts and websites.
Digital tools that allow multiple people to work on the same document or project in real time from different locations, such as shared online documents or project management software.
The method used to deliver digital communications to an audience, such as email, cloud services, messaging apps, mobile apps, multimedia platforms, VoIP services or websites.
